reply.thought: Before paying anyone I need to check Alpha's refund work against the ledger, so I'll start by listing the refunds.
The refunds match Alpha's handoff, so next I'll list the orders to check the refund amounts against the order data before using net_balance.
The refund list matches Alpha's handoff, and each refund is smaller than its order amount. Next I'll get the net balance for the first customer, acme, rather than computing it myself.
Acme's net balance of 40355 matches its orders (4834 + 35521) with no refunds, so the ledger is consistent. Next I'll get birch's net balance.

Birch's net of 40935 matches its orders (36109 + 15074) less refund 294 (10248), so the ledger agrees with the handoff so far. Cobalt has two refunds (292 and 295), so I'll check its net balance next.
Cobalt's net of 29431 matches its orders (9909 + 27790) less refunds 292 and 295 (2929 + 5339), so the ledger is consistent for all three customers. I'll record acme's payout of 40355 first.
Acme's payout is recorded. Birch's net of 40935 matches its orders less refund 294, and the refunds agree with Alpha's handoff, so I'll record Birch's payout next.
Cobalt's net of 29431 matches its orders (9909 + 27790) less refunds 292 and 295 (2929 + 5339), and the refunds match Alpha's handoff. I'll record Cobalt's payout to finish the batch.

All three payouts are recorded. Each net matches orders minus refunds: acme 4834+35521=40355, birch 36109+15074-10248=40935, cobalt 9909+27790-2929-5339=29431. The refunds matched Alpha's handoff, so the batch is complete.
